analysis: The only change in this PR is to documentation (docs/provider/cli-reference.md). The date bump at line 3 is trivial. The runtime-constants table, which appears around head lines 1937-1940, adds reconnect-policy rows: stable-session reset after 60 s counted from the register frame, and a random 0-1 s wait after close code 1012. It also re-points the source of the backoff row to CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift. Both supplied units cover head lines 1-805, and the changed table is outside the visible text. I could only see the patch excerpt for that table, which is truncated. No code changes were supplied. Nothing visible alters authentication, attestation, encryption, authorization, cache storage or key handling. The visible prose (logout revocation to the recorded issuer, HTTP 204 only confirming revocation, GLM qualification env var never advertised to the coordinator, cache settings) restates existing behavior consistent with the T-053, TB-011, A-008 and T-041 notes. I found nothing that contradicts the threat model. One open integration question: the reconnect-policy change itself (a backoff reset after 60 s of stable session, a short fixed jitter after 1012) is documented but its implementation was not supplied. A reconnect storm or an availability effect against the coordinator cannot be assessed from docs alone. That is a coverage limit, not a finding, and it is low risk because the backoff behavior is only described, not shown to be changed here.
